role: formal language in the logical-system triple
scope: P1 formal-language component before signature specialization
notes: A set of finite grammatical expressions in the explicit definition of a logical system; the source-local reading is recalled in \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-language-filter-readings}. The first-order specialization later declares a signature separately.

role: proper filter of subsets in the inherited Ultrafilter Lemma
scope: P1 proper filter in the inherited Ultrafilter Lemma
notes: The four displayed closure and properness conditions define a filter on the set \(I\). This occurrence precedes and has a different type from the function-symbol family of a signature.

role: domain of the structure in the inherited register and substitution solution
scope: Inherited domain bars in the notation register and substitution solution
notes: The register calls the result a set and names it the domain. The substitution proof quantifies assignment values in that same carrier; its restoration-only structure macro prints this letter. No cardinality is asserted.

role: displayed register entries for input and tape alphabets
scope: Inherited register mentions of machine alphabets and calculi
notes: The inherited table explicitly limits the alphabet role to Turing-machine definitions. These are quoted symbol entries, not formula contexts in the notation appendix.

role: displayed register entry for a derivation calculus
scope: Inherited register mentions of machine alphabets and calculi
notes: The inherited derivability row prints the calculus as a subscript and explicitly requires that calculus to have been declared.

role: set ultrafilter extending the finite-constraint filter
notes: An ultrafilter of subsets of the valuation set \(X\); Boolean and propositional compactness proofs take truth sets as its members.

role: poset of proper Boolean-filter extensions
notes: The members are proper filters on the fixed Boolean algebra extending the given filter; the order is inclusion.

role: chain of proper Boolean-filter extensions
notes: A chain in the displayed poset of proper filters; its union is an upper bound and remains proper.

role: class of expanded structures satisfying the added axiom
notes: The proof uses the body declaration: structures for the enlarged signature satisfying \(A=\forall x(x=c\lor R(c,x))\). Restricting to this class yields the stated nonconservative consequence.

role: calculus component of a logical system
notes: The opening and closing comparisons recall the calculus component of the logical-system triple, holding the language fixed while the calculus or semantics changes.

role: choice tower and its least intersection tower
scope: P1 choice towers in the well-ordering proof and finite example
notes: Towers are families of subsets closed under the fixed choice successor and unions; the subscript-zero tower is their intersection. The finite example gives its explicit chain.

role: subfamily whose union lies in a choice tower
notes: A subfamily of a tower, or of its comparable-member subfamily, used in the union-closure condition. It is not a semantics.

role: auxiliary choice tower
notes: A tower contained in the least tower, including the family \(\mathcal U_C\) defined by comparability with a fixed member and its choice successor; minimality forces equality with the least tower.

role: comparable-member subfamily of the least choice tower
notes: Members are the subsets comparable by inclusion with every member of the least tower. Showing this subfamily is itself a tower proves total ordering.

role: proper ultrafilter on the fixed set
notes: The proof inherits the body definition: a proper filter deciding every subset against its complement; the extension and side-condition arguments retain this same type.

role: family of subsets used to generate a proper filter
notes: The upward closure of finite intersections is proper exactly when the generating family has the finite intersection property. Superscript upward-arrow denotes that generated family.

role: two-element CPL truth-value set
notes: The finite check ranges over valuations in \(\{F,T\}^P\); the blackboard letter is that two-element truth-value set.

role: class of permitted Kripke frames
notes: The model must be based on a frame in this class. The local/global entailment and satisfiability passages retain that frame-class parameter; the counterexample proof takes all frames.

role: selected natural-deduction calculus
notes: The named CPL or FOL natural-deduction calculus governs derivability, contexts, structural properties and discharge. This role is separate from the frame-class parameter in the modal passages.

role: semantics with the stated classical negation clause
notes: The permitted semantic data and satisfaction relation determine consequence. The reduction to unsatisfiability uses its classical-negation hypothesis, not a choice of calculus.

role: semantics for the fixed formula language in consistency comparisons
notes: The annex explicitly inherits the fixed semantics and permitted data from its body. Satisfaction, soundness, completeness and the adequate-calculus equivalences all use this semantics.

role: calculus and explicitly specified comparison calculi
notes: The structural consistency arguments use the selected calculus. The later decorated calculi are Horn-rule closures and the named separating examples; they retain the calculus type and their distinct rule sets.

role: class of permitted semantic data
scope: P1 consistency proof permitted semantic data
notes: The class is supplied by the fixed semantics. Its nonemptiness is the hypothesis used for consistency of the empty context; it is not a derivation collection.

role: displayed category notation in the source-scope comparison
notes: The selected table quotes the category of arrow-only typed contexts under the P10 cartesian-lambda scope. The mention convention is \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-register-mentions}.

role: displayed scoped blackboard-letter specimen
notes: The comparison distinguishes CPL truth values, a complete Boolean algebra, and Boolean quotients of formulas. These are typed mentions under \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-register-mentions}; the rank-table Boolean operations, where present, retain their printed P6 scope.

role: displayed scoped blackboard-letter specimen
notes: The comparison distinguishes the two-element field, finite-ordinal category and reduction strategy. These are typed mentions under \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-register-mentions}; the rank-table Boolean operations, where present, retain their printed P6 scope.

role: displayed scoped blackboard-letter specimen
notes: The comparison distinguishes a forcing poset from a probability measure. These are typed mentions under \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-register-mentions}; the rank-table Boolean operations, where present, retain their printed P6 scope.

role: displayed scoped blackboard-letter specimen
notes: The comparison names the expectation operator in its declared probability scopes. These are typed mentions under \cref{def:p01-w02-p01-024-register-mentions}; the rank-table Boolean operations, where present, retain their printed P6 scope.

role: displayed ordinal-notation-system index in the rank table
notes: The index belongs to the printed P4 ordinal-notation order operators. The table mentions those source-scoped operators, without introducing an ordinal-notation system in P1.

role: two-element truth-value set in the functional-completeness discussion
notes: The cited CPL convention supplies \(\{F,T\}\). The display ranges over functions of each finite arity on this set, before separating nullary and positive-arity completeness.

role: type universe for the motive-family examples
notes: The codomain of the displayed dependent type families and the ambient universe of the HoTT elimination examples. Source-specific eliminators retain their stated motives, branch data and computation rules.
